title: Algebraic Modelings of the Supersingular Isogeny Problem
summary: We present a new algebraic modeling of the Supersingular Isogeny Problem as a system of multivariate polynomial equations, in the case where the elliptic curves are connected by an isogeny whose degree is a power of $2$ or $3$. This modeling relies on Renes formulas for elliptic curves in Montgomery form (degree $2$) or triangular form (degree $3$). We investigate several algebraic properties of these systems: we prove that they are zero-dimensional, compute the dimension of their highest degree part, and show that they are not in generic coordinates.
